quantContext.note: From this project's own scoring pipeline (companies.json + screener.js). Included for reference only - not itself a research source.

whyCheapBearCase.answer: CHTR trades at an extremely low P/E (3.98) and P/B (1.08) despite a strong ROE (29.42%) [source: 1], and the filing evidence points to real, structural reasons for the discount rather than pure mispricing. First, leverage is severe: total debt principal was $94.6 billion as of December 31, 2025 (a mix of credit-facility debt, investment-grade senior secured notes, and high-yield senior unsecured notes), against a debt/equity ratio of 6.007 [source: 1, 4]. Second, the core wired subscriber base is shrinking: residential Internet customers fell 510,000, residential video customers fell 77,000, and residential wireline voice customers fell 667,000 year-over-year through June 30, 2026 [source: 2]. Third, and most concretely, management itself flags a forward impairment risk tied directly to the stock price: 'Considering the decline in Charter's stock price during the quarter ending June 30, 2026, we continue to monitor factors that could impact the fair value of our franchises and goodwill... if the lower stock price persists, we may need to... perform a quantitative impairment assessment' [source: 2]. Franchise intangibles (~$67.5 billion) and goodwill (~$29.7 billion) together were roughly 63% of total assets as of the 10-K date [source: 4] - not a trivial exposure. Finally, the company is mid-integration on the $34 billion Cox Communications transaction, generating real 'transition expenses,' with a cached headline describing visible 'tensions' as the deal nears close [source: 6].

revenueEpsTrend.answer: Mixed - revenue and net income are both declining while diluted EPS is rising, and the filing explains why. Total revenue fell $240 million (-1.7%) in Q2 2026 to $13,526M from $13,766M in Q2 2025, and fell $378 million (-1.4%) for H1 2026 ($27,123M vs $27,501M); full-year FY2025 revenue was $54,774M vs $55,085M in FY2024 (-0.6%) [source: 2, 4, 5]. Net income attributable to Charter shareholders was down $9 million (-0.7%) in Q2 2026 ($1,292M vs $1,301M) and down $63 million (-2.5%) for H1 2026 ($2,455M vs $2,518M); FY2025 was $4,987M vs $5,083M in FY2024 (-1.9%) [source: 2, 4, 5]. Yet diluted EPS rose to $10.66 in Q2 2026 from $9.18 in Q2 2025 (+16.1%), and to $19.81 for H1 2026 from $17.59 in H1 2025 (+12.6%) [source: 2, 5] - almost entirely a function of an aggressive buyback: diluted weighted-average shares outstanding fell from 141,684,415 (Q2 2025) to 121,255,667 (Q2 2026), a 14.4% reduction [source: 2]. This is a case where per-share metrics look strong while the underlying revenue and net-income base is shrinking - the buyback is real and substantial, but it is masking, not reversing, top-line and bottom-line contraction.

marginTrend.answer: Slightly compressing. Operating margin (income from operations / revenue) was 22.65% in Q2 2026 ($3,063M / $13,526M) versus 23.82% in Q2 2025 ($3,279M / $13,766M), down about 1.17 points; for H1 2026 it was 23.12% ($6,271M / $27,123M) versus 23.69% in H1 2025 ($6,516M / $27,501M), down about 0.57 points; full-year FY2025 was 23.57% ($12,908M / $54,774M) versus 23.81% in FY2024 ($13,118M / $55,085M), down about 0.24 points - consistent with this project's own companyMetrics marginTrend figure of -0.24 [source: 1, 2, 4]. The MD&A attributes cost pressure partly to higher mobile service direct costs and mobile device sales as mobile lines grow, and to Cox-integration 'transition expenses,' partially offset by declining programming costs as a share of total operating costs (25% of total operating costs and expenses in Q2 2026 versus 27% in Q2 2025) [source: 2].

guidanceChange.answer: Not determinable from available sources. The extracted MD&A text (Results of Operations, Adjusted EBITDA/free cash flow reconciliation, liquidity overview) does not contain an explicit forward-looking revenue, EPS, or Adjusted EBITDA guidance range for FY2026, and none of the cached news headlines for CHTR discuss management guidance directly - they cover Cox deal progress and recent debt issuance/exchange activity instead [source: 6, 7, 8]. I did not locate an earnings-call transcript or guidance press release in the sources available to this pipeline, so I am not answering this from general knowledge.

catalysts.text: The $34 billion Cox Communications acquisition ('the Cox Transactions') is reportedly nearing completion per a recent headline, and the 10-Q's ongoing 'transition expenses' plus the 10-K's related-party GCI Divestiture disclosure both confirm the deal is live and being actively integrated, not just announced.

Mobile is the clear growth engine: mobile service revenue rose 18.9% YoY in Q2 2026 ($1,095M vs $921M) on roughly 1.6 million net residential mobile line adds, partially offsetting declines in legacy Internet, video, and voice.

Large, active share repurchase program: Charter bought back approximately 4.0 million Class A shares for approximately $838 million in Q2 2026 alone, with $365 million of remaining board authorization as of quarter-end, directly supporting per-share earnings metrics.

Active refinancing of the debt stack: Charter priced $4.75 billion of new senior secured notes and announced pricing terms for a debt exchange offer in early August 2026, extending maturities ahead of the elevated leverage becoming a nearer-term issue.

risks.text: Management has explicitly disclosed a forward-looking impairment risk tied to Charter's declining stock price: franchise intangibles (~$67.5 billion) and goodwill (~$29.7 billion) together are roughly 63% of total assets, and a quantitative impairment assessment may be required if the lower stock price persists.

Severe balance-sheet leverage: $94.6 billion of total debt principal as of December 31, 2025 (debt/equity 6.007 per this project's data), with continued large note issuances and exchange offers in August 2026 - necessary refinancing activity that nonetheless underscores dependence on continued capital-markets access.

Secular decline in the core residential subscriber base: Internet customers down 510,000, video customers down 77,000, and wireline voice customers down 667,000 year-over-year through Q2 2026; the 10-K's Risk Factors text separately warns that competition 'may also reduce our expected growth of future cash flows which may contribute to future impairments of our franchises and goodwill,' directly linking subscriber losses to the impairment risk above.

Cox integration execution risk: a cached headline explicitly describes 'tensions' as the $34 billion deal nears its finish line, alongside real transition expenses already being incurred ($65 million and $89 million for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026, respectively).

verdict.reasoning: The filing evidence shows a company that is statistically very cheap (P/E 3.98, ROE 29.42%) for reasons that are real and filing-confirmed, not just sentiment noise: revenue and net income are both declining (-1.4% and -2.5% for H1 2026, respectively), the core wired subscriber base is shrinking across every legacy product line, leverage is extreme ($94.6B debt, debt/equity 6.007), and management itself has flagged a real risk of a future non-cash impairment charge on nearly $97 billion of combined franchise/goodwill intangibles tied directly to the stock's own price decline [source: 1, 2, 4]. That combination - a company voluntarily disclosing that its own market price could trigger a future write-down of the majority of its balance sheet - is a materially more specific and concerning signal than a plain low P/E. Offsetting this, diluted EPS is growing double digits via a large, real buyback, mobile service revenue is genuinely growing (+18.9% YoY), programming cost efficiency is improving, and the $34 billion Cox acquisition could eventually restore scale-driven growth [source: 2, 3, 6]. Given the buyback-masked earnings decline, the structural subscriber erosion, and the company's own explicit impairment-risk disclosure, this leans toward 'possible value trap' rather than a clean opportunity, but confidence is only medium because the EPS/mobile/Cox offsets are also real and could change the trajectory over the next several quarters.
